concepts.definition: Estimating a one-minute value by counting for a short time and multiplying the result.
concepts.example: If you count 14 beats in 10 seconds, you get 14 x 6 = 84 beats per minute.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting the multiplier: the number of beats stays on the screen, not the beats per minute.

concepts.definition: A variable that holds 0 or 1 and answers the question "is this action valid right now?".
concepts.example: While olcum = 1, A counts; while olcum = 0, A does nothing.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to set the flag to 1: the measurement never starts and A never counts.

concepts.definition: The pause block only stops its own hat block; the other hat blocks keep running.
concepts.example: While B waits for 10 seconds, button A keeps counting presses.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the pause block stops the whole card.

concepts.definition: Setting the counter to 0 at the start of a new measurement.
concepts.example: The first block of the B hat block is set sayac to 0.
concepts.pitfall: Not resetting: in the second measurement the earlier beats are added too, and the result is inflated.

concepts.definition: The unit of the pause block; 1000 ms = 1 second.
concepts.example: For 10 seconds you write pause [10000] ms.
concepts.pitfall: Writing pause [10]: this is only 10 ms, which you cannot notice by eye.

quiz.prompt: On the pulse meter you counted 14 beats in 10 seconds. Which number should the card show?
quiz.explanation: 6 times 10 seconds is one minute. 14 x 6 = 84. Showing the number of beats (14) or multiplying by 10 (140) does not give the beats per minute.

quiz.prompt: If button A is pressed while the B hat block is waiting at the pause [10000] ms block, what happens?
options: Button A does not work, because the card is waiting
The A hat block runs, because hat blocks carry on independently of each other
The A presses are handled all together after 10 seconds
quiz.explanation: pause only stops its own hat block. The A hat block is a separate task and runs straight away on every press. That is why counting can happen while waiting.

quiz.prompt:
This program always shows 0, even if A is pressed 12 times in 10 seconds. Which is the mistake?

```
on button B pressed:
  set sayac to 0
  pause 10000 ms
  set olcum to 1
  show number (sayac x 6)

on button A pressed:
  if olcum = 1 then:
    change sayac by 1
```
options: In the A hat block, sayac should go up by 2 instead of 1
The set olcum to 1 block comes after the pause block; because olcum is 0 during the wait, A never counts
sayac was not reset at the start
quiz.explanation: The flag must be set to 1 before the wait starts. Here it becomes 1 after the wait has finished, so the counting window never opens and sayac stays 0. The multiplier and the reset are correct.

quiz.prompt:
The program below is used. 12 beats were counted in the first measurement, and right after that 9 beats in the second measurement. What does the card show at the end of the second measurement?

```
on start:
  set sayac to 0
  set olcum to 0

on button B pressed:
  set olcum to 1
  pause 10000 ms
  set olcum to 0
  show number (sayac x 6)

on button A pressed:
  if olcum = 1 then:
    change sayac by 1
```
quiz.explanation: The program does not reset sayac in B. In the second measurement sayac becomes 12 + 9 = 21, and 21 x 6 = 126 is shown. 54 would be the result of the second measurement alone; but there is no reset.

quiz.prompt: You increased the measurement time to 15 seconds and made the multiplier 4. You counted 17 beats in 15 seconds. How many beats per minute is that?
quiz.explanation: 4 times 15 seconds is 60 seconds. 17 x 4 = 68. The multiplier is chosen from the time: time x multiplier = 60.
